findings.summary: DdControlPlane.recover returns resume.resumed = true without re-entering the suspended thread: unlike gate(resume=True), which calls _launch(record, resume=True), recover only calls HumanRecoveryExit.resume, which returns a payload. No path outside recover/recoveries/status/evidence reads the recovery trail, so the sealed decision does not gate the actual relaunch, and the tool's own docstring ('resumes the suspended work from that recorded decision alone') overstates the effect. The spec's authenticate / record-with-target / only-from-the-record obligations are met -- the resume gate genuinely refuses without a record -- but an operator reading the MCP response would believe a suspended development was resumed when it was not.

No test asserts that DdControlPlane.create refuses an out-of-scope spec with SCOPE_BOUNDARY_VIOLATION. B1's refusal is covered at the scope module (tests/test_scope_isolation.py), on the dispatch/handoff path (tests/test_dispatch.py:210), and for the quarantine helper (tests/test_dd_b2_recovery.py:375), but the admission path -- the one that persists scope_verdict as the B3 scope evidence -- has only its success case exercised, so a regression that dropped the _require_scope call from create would not be caught by name.

The committed implement handoff records work_head_commit as d03448376c03f7835eb2240efea5ecd7d2ac194f, while the attempt context supplied to this review names the product commit (work_head_commit) as 235a6eb4f6e7cadf9709bdbe5ef4587818fc1389. This is consistent with the materializer stacking a metadata-only commit on the actor's product commit, but the same field name carries different SHAs in the two records. The identical disagreement was raised on attempts 1 and 2 of earlier generations and has not been reconciled.

The receipt-level scope check is annotation-only: _sealed_receipt attaches a scope_violations key to the assembled evidence entry but neither rejects the receipt nor moves it out of the chain, so 'quarantine' here means 'labelled in the evidence output'. The hard refusals live at admission (create) and on the dispatch path (read_committed_refs); the entries do carry the boundary's reference, label and excerpt, so the annotation is at least attributable.

B2 adoption is automatic and idempotent once a discovery batch arrives, but nothing in src/ discovers: AdoptionLedger.discover is called only from DdControlPlane.adopt, which takes the batch from its caller, and development_adopt is the only entry point. The spec's trigger ('when eligible work is discovered') is therefore satisfied by the caller rather than by an in-repo scanner. The discovery-then-adopt split and its idempotency -- what the spec and B3's mandated test list actually require -- are implemented and tested over the real MCP surface. Carried forward from the same note on attempt 2 of an earlier generation.

EvidenceChain.validate returns no reasons for an empty link tuple, so b3_evidence_chain reports valid = true for a development whose scope_verdict is absent and whose adoption and recovery trails are empty. Each link's internal completeness (removed phenomenon/mechanism/evidence, substituted mechanism, missing target) is checked and tested, which is the spec's phenomenon->mechanism->evidence reading; the assembly level simply has no floor on how many behaviours must be present.

Two mechanical checks were not executed, because this reviewer role has file-inspection tools only: the mandated product-consistency diff between 235a6eb4 and fb8f93e2 excluding .dev-dispatch, and the spec's acceptance commands (uv sync --frozen, make verify). No claim is made about either. The implement handoff's verification_record attests exit_code 0 for both commands with 1270 of 1271 tests passed, and the review was conducted against the worktree contents at /data/worktrees/fleet-graph-b1-b3-20260828. No finding is raised on this basis.
